directAnswer: To clear the DNS cache on Windows 11, open Command Prompt as an administrator and enter 'ipconfig /flushdns'.
summary: Clearing the DNS cache on Windows 11 helps resolve connectivity issues by removing outdated or corrupted DNS records.

sections.heading: Why Clear DNS Cache?
sections.body: Clearing the DNS cache can resolve network issues, enhance security, and ensure your system uses the most current DNS information.

sections.heading: How DNS Cache Works
sections.body: The DNS cache stores IP addresses of web servers for recently accessed websites, speeding up future visits by reducing DNS server queries.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting DNS Issues
sections.body: If you experience slow browsing or can't access certain websites, clearing the DNS cache may fix these issues by removing outdated DNS records.

steps.title: Open Command Prompt as Administrator
steps.detail: Press 'Win + X' and select 'Windows Terminal (Admin)' from the menu. If 'Command Prompt (Admin)' is available, you can select that instead.

steps.title: Confirm User Account Control
steps.detail: If prompted by User Account Control, click 'Yes' to allow changes to your device.

steps.title: Type the DNS Flush Command
steps.detail: In the Command Prompt window, type 'ipconfig /flushdns' and press 'Enter'.

steps.title: Verify DNS Cache Clearance
steps.detail: Look for the confirmation message 'Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache'.

faqs.question: What is DNS cache?
faqs.answer: DNS cache is a temporary database on your computer that stores records of recent visits to websites and internet domains.

faqs.question: How often should I clear my DNS cache?
faqs.answer: Clearing the DNS cache is not regularly necessary but can be helpful if you experience connectivity issues or after DNS changes.

faqs.question: Does clearing DNS cache affect browsing history?
faqs.answer: No, clearing the DNS cache does not affect your browsing history; it only removes stored DNS records.

caveats: Some network configurations may require additional steps.
Clearing the DNS cache does not directly affect internet speed.
DNS cache may rebuild over time, requiring periodic clearance if issues persist.
